name: Planned humanoid service robots at Suvarnabhumi Airport (Sky ICT)
summary: Sky ICT, a SET-listed aviation technology provider in Thailand, plans to pilot humanoid service robots at Suvarnabhumi Airport toward the end of 2026, ASEAN NOW reported on November 5. Chief executive Sithidej Mayalarp said humanoid robots could give passengers information and directions, and that more conventional robots could move baggage and parcels along airport conveyor systems. The company frames the trial inside a three-stage shift: shared aviation data for prediction, AI for personalized services and preventive maintenance, then broader autonomous airport operations with biometrics and robots. Sky ICT has not said whether the trial will replace staff or change passenger procedures, and no robot maker, count or cost was named. This is a planned pilot, not a live deployment.

whyItMatters: Passenger questions and short bag moves eat staff time at peak banks, and a robot that answers directions or feeds a conveyor can free people for exceptions. Because this trial is still ahead, watch for who supplies the robots and what success looks like before you budget one. If you run a terminal or cargo shed, count how many of your peak-hour tasks are pure information or short tote moves, because those are the first robotics candidates.
